summary: The paper proposes LayerBudget, a training-free online allocator that jointly picks a per-layer token-retention count n_l and KV bit-width b_l under a global byte budget, using a greedy marginal-gain solver over a hand-built quality model Q = coverage x fidelity x importance. It reports WikiText-2 PPL ratios across 7 models (7B-72B), 17 reimplemented baselines, MMLU/GSM8K/NIAH/RULER/LongBench, and 16K-32K context. Reading strictly in page order with no author context, the document is difficult to trust: the abstract ends mid-sentence, roughly thirty numeric claims terminate immediately after a percent sign, one section header and one table environment are syntactically unclosed, and the Limitations section has no heading. Beneath the presentation problems the numbers do not agree with each other: the same cell (Llama-2-7B, 1024 tokens, mean-fill, 6x) is reported as 1.099 (Table 1), 1.17 (Table 2), and 1.13 (Section 6); the tables labelled 'LayerBudget' in the component and deployment ablations carry the value the importance ablation assigns to the non-default sigmoid variant; the memory table at 'CR=2x' shows effective compressions of 1.32x, 3.5x, and 1.76x; and the abstract's load-bearing qualifier 'at memory-matched comparison' points to an appendix that does not exist in the submission. Most seriously, the paper's own tables show the method tying or losing to KIVI, a 2024 quantization baseline, on every metric at every scale, including a direct memory-matched loss (LayerBudget 12,939 KB / 1.07 vs KIVI 9,990 KB / 1.01 at nominal 6x), and the paper's central 'quantize first, evict last' mechanism is contradicted by its own Eq. 2/3 plus its own Appendix D constants. I recommend rejection.
strengths: The comparison surface is unusually broad for this literature: 17 baselines reimplemented behind a single interface, 7 models spanning MHA and GQA from 7B to 72B, and 8 evaluation tasks, all against a single explicitly stated denominator (Section 4, 'CR = Full_KV_bytes / method_KV_bytes'). Defining CR as a method-agnostic byte ratio rather than a token-count ratio is the correct axis and most papers in this space do not do it.

The mean-fill ablation (Section 6) is a cheap, transferable, well-controlled result: logits KL 0.249 -> 0.009 on Mistral-7B and 0.6696 -> 0.0636 on Llama-2-7B at 6x, with median-fill and random-fill (matched mean/std) run as controls to isolate first-moment preservation as the operative mechanism. This is the one component of the paper whose causal story is actually tested rather than asserted.

The complexity accounting for the allocator is done carefully and honestly separated from the profiling cost: Section 3.4 gives O(L * S/dn) inner-loop iterations, measures <1 ms in isolation on Mistral-7B at S=1024, extrapolates to ~10 ms for Qwen2.5-72B at 32K, and explicitly states that the 100-513 ms figure in the overhead table is the full profiling pipeline (Gini extraction across all layers) rather than the allocator. Many efficiency papers conflate exactly these two costs.

The 32K long-context result is a useful negative result about the baseline family: H2O degrading to 83.4x PPL at 4x/32K on Mistral-7B (Table 21) while StreamingLLM stays at 1.026 is a concrete, reproducible failure-mode datapoint that the community can use independently of whether LayerBudget itself is adopted.

The H2O reimplementation sanity check described in the MMLU table caption (a faithful per-head H2O matching the official FMInference/H2O algorithm with recent_ratio=0.1) is the right methodological instinct: when a baseline collapses, check the reimplementation before reporting the collapse.
weaknesses: FATAL (fatal-flaw gate (a)): the method does not beat the fairest and simplest strong baseline on the metric that matters. In Table 2, KIVI is flat at 1.01-1.02 on all four 7B-8B models at all CRs while LayerBudget is 1.00/1.01/1.03/1.25 (Mistral) and 1.00/1.02/1.02/1.17 (Llama-2-7B) - i.e. LayerBudget wins only at 2x by 0.01-0.02 (well inside a 6-chunk sample), ties at 3-4x, and loses badly at 6x. Table 12 (13B-14B): KIVI 1.02/1.02/1.02/1.02 vs LayerBudget 1.00/1.01/1.11/1.56 on Llama-2-13B - KIVI wins at 4x and 6x. Table 22 (72B): KIVI 1.00/1.00/1.00/1.00 vs LayerBudget 1.00/1.00/1.00/1.06, and on RULER@4096 KIVI 99/100 vs LayerBudget 98/100 - KIVI wins at 2x. Table 15 is a direct memory-matched loss: at nominal 6x on Mistral-7B, LayerBudget uses 12,939 KB for PPL 1.07 while KIVI uses 9,990 KB for PPL 1.01, i.e. 29.5% more memory for 6% worse quality. Appendix E's 'the 2x inflation is fixed across methods' defence does not rescue this, because it is a uniform multiplier applied to both rows. The paper's own component ablation (Table 17) closes the case: Joint (Ours) 1.00/3.23 and 1.02/45.09 versus Quant only 1.00/1.00 and 1.02/1.01 at 3x/6x - the joint allocator is never better than doing nothing but INT4, and at 6x it is also worse than Eviction only (3.18 / 44.71). Fix: either demonstrate a regime where the joint allocation strictly dominates INT4-everywhere at matched bytes, or retract the central claim.

The abstract's escape hatch for the KIVI comparison - 'ranks first among token-compression methods at 2-4x at memory-matched comparison' - is unsupported by any table in the submission. Section 4 promises 'we report a memory-matched comparison in Appendix [REF]'; Table 17's caption asserts 'Under a memory-matched comparison (Appendix [REF]), quant-only at ~6x requires evicting tokens beyond the INT4 floor and degrades comparably'. No such appendix exists: the appendices are A (pseudocode), B (positioning), C (LB-KV), D (fidelity calibration), E (byte-CR reconciliation), F (additional results), and none of them contains a memory-matched quant-only sweep. A headline qualifier whose evidence is cited twice and shipped zero times is not a presentation slip; it is the missing experiment on which the paper's only defence against KIVI rests. Fix: run quant-only (INT4 + eviction past the INT4 floor) at matched mean_memory_bytes against LayerBudget at 3x/4x/6x and report it.

The paper's central mechanism claim is contradicted by the paper's own equations and constants (recomputed, see P3). Section 3.5 states that 'at low CR, dQ/dM for a bit-upgrade exceeds that of a token-add at almost every layer'. From Eq. 2-3: for a 4->8 upgrade dM = M and dQ = Q*(F(8)-F(4))/F(4); for a token-add dM = M*dn/n and dQ ~ Q*(1-g_l)*dn/n. Gain-per-byte ratio (token-add / bit-upgrade) = (1-g_l)*F(4)/(F(8)-F(4)). With Appendix D's Mistral values (F(8)=0.9998, F(4)=0.9794) this is 48*(1-g_l), which is 3.4x at the paper's maximum reported Gini (0.93) and 27x at its minimum (0.43). Token-adds strictly dominate bit-upgrades at every layer under the paper's own model, so the stated 'quantize first' behaviour cannot 'emerge naturally from the marginal gains' - it must come from the b_min=4 initialization or from code that differs from Eq. 2-3. Relatedly, Section 3.5's concavity argument quotes dF(4->8) = 0.0035, but Appendix D gives 0.9998-0.9794 = 0.0204 for Mistral and 0.9997-0.9758 = 0.0239 for Llama-2-7B - the quoted constant is off by 6x and is stale relative to the paper's own calibration table. Fix: reconcile the implementation with Eq. 2-3, and ablate the allocator initialized at b=16 to show quantize-first is a discovered property rather than an initialization artifact.

Three tables give three different values for the same experimental cell, and the component/deployment ablations appear to be running a configuration the paper says is not the method. Llama-2-7B, 1024 tokens, mean-fill, 6x: Table 1 says 1.099, Table 2 says 1.17, Section 6 says 1.13. Llama-2-7B at 3x: Table 1 says 1.004, Table 2 says 1.02. Worse, Table 5 (importance ablation, 512 tokens, zero-fill) reports the inverted default at 2.52 on Llama-2-7B at 6x and the sigmoid variant at 45.09 - but Tables 17, 18 and 19, all labelled 'LayerBudget'/'Joint (Ours)' and all zero-fill, report 45.09 and 3.23, exactly Table 5's sigmoid-row values, not the inverted-default values (2.52 / 1.283). Either those tables were produced with the non-default importance direction or the labels are wrong. This directly contaminates the mean-fill contribution: Section 6's '45.09 to 1.13 at 6x (97.5%)' credits mean-fill with an improvement measured against the sigmoid configuration, not against the method's own zero-fill default of 2.52. Fix: state the exact (importance direction, fill, seq_len, backend) tuple in every table caption and regenerate the ablations under the default.

The abstract's headline number is contradicted by the paper's own tables in two places. (i) 'LayerBudget achieves PPL ratio <=1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' - Table 12 reports 1.11 at 4x on Llama-2-13B and 1.56 at 6x. The parenthetical '<=1.01 on 13B-72B at GQA' silently carves out the one 13B MHA model that breaks the claim, which is exactly the kind of qualifier a reader only notices on the second pass. (ii) Section 6 states 'at CR=4x and 4096 tokens, LayerBudget matches Full KV accuracy on every model (100...' while Table 13 shows Mistral-7B Full KV 86.7 and LayerBudget at 4x = 73.3 - a 13.4-point drop on the model the paper otherwise foregrounds. The abstract's NIAH sentence is truncated but appears to make the same claim. Fix: state the claim over the set of models it is actually true for.

The memory table (Table 16), captioned 'KV cache memory savings at CR=2x', reports effective compressions of 1.32x (Llama-2-7B: 287 -> 218 MB, 24.3%), 3.5x (Llama-3.1-8B: 189 -> 54 MB, 71.2%), and 1.76x (Mistral-7B: 95 -> 54 MB, 42.9%). None of these is 2x, and this directly contradicts Appendix E's audit claim that 'every method's effective CR matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05'. The same table is internally impossible: Section 4 lists Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B as identical KV geometries (32 layers, 8 KV heads), and the LB KV column agrees (54 MB / 109 MB / 435 MB for both), yet their Base KV columns differ by exactly 2x (95 vs 189 MB at 512 tokens). The correct FP16 value for that geometry is 2*32*512*8*128*2 = 67.1 MB, which matches neither. Fix: recompute the base-KV column from the model configs and re-derive the savings.

The only broad long-context downstream benchmark is at the noise floor and is therefore uninformative. Table 10 reports LongBench overall scores of 0.056 / 0.040 / 0.050 for Full KV on Mistral-7B / Llama-3.1-8B / Llama-2-7B. A Full-KV model scoring 0.05 on LongBench mean F1/ROUGE-L means the harness is producing essentially no task performance for the uncompressed reference, so 'LayerBudget matches Full KV on all models' (0.055 / 0.040 / 0.050) is a statement about a broken measurement, not about compression quality. The caption's own footnote ('H2O on Llama-2-7B anomalously high due to degenerate repetition inflating F1', H2O 0.097 vs Full KV 0.050) confirms the metric is not tracking quality. Separately, LongBench-v1 is run at 4096 tokens, truncating most of its tasks. Fix: rerun on LongBench-v2 or RULER at the full context lengths with a sanity-checked Full-KV reference before making any downstream claim.

Several baselines are almost certainly misconfigured, which undermines the ranking claim that is the paper's contribution 4. In Table 20, SnapKV scores 27.1 / 29.6 / 29.4 / 33.4 / 41.2 on MMLU against Full KV 47.3 / 63.9 / 60.2 / 72.9 / 76.6 - at or below four-choice chance on three models, at compression ratios where SnapKV is published as near-lossless. The paper defends the H2O collapse with a reimplementation check but offers no such check for SnapKV. In Table 2, DuoAttn is identical across all four CRs (1.22/1.22/1.22/1.22 on Llama-2-7B) and MiniKV is identical at 2/3/4x, meaning those baselines were evaluated once and copied across the budget sweep rather than swept. And KIVI's flat row means that at nominal 2x and 3x, KIVI is actually delivering ~4x compression - i.e. it is using roughly half the byte budget LayerBudget is given and still matching it. Fix: verify each baseline against its published numbers on at least one shared setting, and either sweep the flat rows or mark those cells as budget-insensitive by construction.

The 'quantize first' claim of ranking primacy is stated as a universal and is false in the paper's own tables. Table 2's caption asserts 'LayerBudget ranks 1st among all token-compression methods at every setting' and Section 4 repeats 'At every configuration across all four models in Table [REF], it outperforms H2O, CAKE, SnapKV, D2O, and Ada-KV'. But in the same table MiniKV beats LayerBudget on Llama-3.1-8B at 6x (1.07 vs 1.08) and ties on Qwen3-8B at 6x (1.03 vs 1.03), and in Table 1 the MoE-nD framing beats LayerBudget on Mistral-7B at 6x (1.038 vs 1.250) - as does the paper's own LB-KV variant (1.062). The paper's Limitation 5 concedes exactly this. A caption whose universal is falsified two rows above it is a defect, not a rounding issue. Fix: restrict the ranking claim to CR <= 4x and to the method set where it holds.

The document as received does not appear to compile, and roughly thirty numeric claims terminate mid-sentence immediately after a percent sign. Concrete syntax faults: line 447 '\begin{table[t]' (unclosed brace on the environment name), line 485 '\section{Analysis' (unclosed brace), line 496 '\textbf{Downstream accuracy.' (unclosed brace). Consequences visible in the text: the abstract ends mid-sentence at 'retains 100'; the Limitations block ('We identify the following limitations') has no section heading and is preceded by a sentence cut off at 'On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]'; contribution 1's headline number reads 'achieving 118--119' with no unit and no object. If the percent truncations are an artifact of the copy I was given, that must be verified against the compiled PDF - but the three unbalanced braces are in the source I was asked to review and would abort the LaTeX run. Fix: compile the submission from a clean directory and read the PDF end to end before submitting.

There is no theorem, lemma, or proof in the section titled 'Theoretical Properties' (Section 3.5). What the section actually contains is: a claim that the objective 'is an instance of' MCKP (asserted, and questionable - MCKP selects exactly one item per class, whereas n_l here is quasi-continuous at step 8 and b_l has three levels, making this a bounded/multi-dimensional knapsack); a paragraph explaining which bound the authors do NOT claim; a statement that an FPTAS exists but is impractical; and one empirical percentage whose object is truncated. A section that argues only for the absence of a guarantee should be folded into the method section, and the MCKP identification should be either proved or dropped.

The quality model Q = C x F x w, which the entire method optimizes, is never validated as a predictor of the quantity the paper reports. C is checked once (attention-mass MAE 3.1% on Mistral-7B only); F is a cosine similarity between quantized and full-precision tensors that is never mapped to PPL or accuracy; w is a hand-chosen sigmoid with k=5, tau=0.3 and no sensitivity analysis, whose direction the paper itself shows is architecture-dependent (early-bottleneck on Mistral, late on Llama-2-13B, flat on Qwen2.5-14B). Multiplying an attention-mass fraction by a cosine similarity by an arbitrary monotone weight yields a scalar in unknown units that is then compared across layers as dQ/dM. Contribution 1's phrase 'calibrated fidelity constants' overstates what Appendix D establishes: F is calibrated as cosine similarity, not calibrated against quality. Fix: show rank correlation between predicted Q and measured PPL/accuracy over a set of allocations, and sweep k and tau.
questions: Table 1 gives LayerBudget on Llama-2-7B at 1024 tokens with mean-fill as 0.996/1.004/1.021/1.099 at 2/3/4/6x; Table 2 gives the same model, context, and fill as 1.00/1.02/1.02/1.17; Section 6 gives 1.13 at 6x. Which is the measurement, and what differs between the runs? Please state the full configuration tuple for each table.

Table 5 reports the inverted default at 2.52 (Llama-2-7B, 6x, zero-fill, 512 tokens) and the sigmoid variant at 45.09, yet Tables 17, 18 and 19 report 'LayerBudget'/'Joint (Ours)' zero-fill at 45.09. Were those three tables produced with sigmoid importance? If so, does the mean-fill improvement in Section 6 (45.09 -> 1.13) survive when measured against the inverted-default zero-fill number of 2.52?

Where is the memory-matched comparison? It is cited in the abstract, in Section 4, and in Table 17's caption, but no appendix in the submission contains it. Please provide the quant-only-past-the-INT4-floor sweep at matched mean_memory_bytes, since it is the paper's only argument against KIVI.

Under Eq. 2-3 and Appendix D's constants, the gain-per-byte of a token-add exceeds that of a 4->8 bit upgrade by a factor of 48*(1-g_l), which is >3x even at your maximum reported Gini of 0.93. How does the implemented allocator produce 'quantize first' behaviour, and what does the allocation look like when initialized at b=16 instead of b_min=4? Also, where does dF(4->8) = 0.0035 in Section 3.5 come from, given Appendix D implies 0.018-0.031?

Table 16 lists Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B as having the same KV geometry (32L, 8 KV heads) and the same compressed size (54 MB at 512 tokens), but base KV sizes of 95 MB and 189 MB. The FP16 value computed from your Section 1 formula is 67.1 MB for both. Which number is right, and does the correction change the 43-72% savings claim?

Full KV scores 0.040-0.056 on LongBench in Table 10. What does that number represent, and why should a reader conclude anything about compression from a benchmark on which the uncompressed model is at the floor? Relatedly, SnapKV is at or below chance on MMLU in Table 20 at 2-4x - has the SnapKV reimplementation been validated against its published MMLU numbers the way H2O was?

Which attention backend and which query-visibility protocol were used for each table? The 32K results specify SDPA; nothing else does. Since the community's matched-budget audits report that sdpa->eager alone shifts RULER by -0.221 and that query-aware vs query-agnostic compression reverses the ranking of SnapKV-style methods, the paper's ranking claim cannot be evaluated without these two facts.

Section 1's motivating number states Llama-2-70B at 8K FP16 'requires over 40 GB'. Your own formula gives 2*80*8192*8*128*2 = 2.68 GB at Llama-2-70B's 8 KV heads (21.5 GB even under a 64-head MHA assumption). What batch size or configuration produces 40 GB?

probe_answers.answer: Alternatives a well-informed reader would expect. (1) KIVI / INT4-everywhere quantization: compared head-to-head in Tables 1, 2, 12, 15, 21, 22 - and it wins or ties essentially everywhere, which the paper handles by inventing the category 'methods that reduce token count' to exclude it (Section 4 bullet 2, contribution 4). Compared, but the comparison is lost and then re-framed. (2) RDKV (rate-distortion bit allocation for joint eviction+quantization, arXiv 2605.08317, May 2026): ignored entirely - not cited, not compared, despite being the same formulation with a principled Lagrangian/reverse-water-filling solver, a fused mixed-bit decode kernel, and 97.81% of full-cache accuracy at 2.48% retention. This is the single closest prior work and its absence is a fatal gap for a paper whose novelty claim is 'no prior online, training-free method jointly optimizes per-layer (n_l, b_l)'. (3) HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, code public): hybrid quantization+eviction with an integrated per-element optimizer - ignored. (4) PolyKV (arXiv 2606.15157): layer-wise design space coupling eviction pattern and capacity - ignored. (5) KVTC (ICLR 2026, NVIDIA) and STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight): both report 20x+ near-lossless compression - ignored, and they set the bar this paper's 2-4x envelope must be judged against. (6) DefensiveKV / Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026), whose Layer- variant is literally per-layer budget allocation and reports RULER-at-20%-cache of 91.4 vs SnapKV 39.0 - ignored. (7) NVIDIA KVPress, the de-facto harness with 30+ methods, PerLayerCompressionPress and QuantizedCache built in - not used and not mentioned, even though the paper's headline methodological contribution is a 17-baseline controlled comparison that KVPress already provides with author-validated implementations. The two 2026 works that ARE engaged (MoE-nD, xKV) are both self-reimplementations from published descriptions, with the paper conceding 'the official artifacts were not public at submission time' and 'we will update against their official code at camera-ready'. Verdict: several obvious alternatives ignored, and the one alternative fully compared beats the method.

Terms/symbols used before definition, overloaded, or never defined - reading strictly in page order. (1) b is overloaded: Section 1 defines it as 'the per-element byte-width' in 2*L*S*H*d*b bytes; Section 3.1 redefines b_l in {4,8,16} as 'the quantization bit-width' and writes M(n,b) = 2*n*H*d*b/8. Same letter, bytes then bits, two pages apart, with no note. (2) CR is used in Related Work ('wins on Llama-2-7B at all four CRs', 'at every CR from 2x to 6x') and in Table 1's caption, several pages before the paragraph 'Compression ratio (CR) definition' in Section 4 that actually defines it. (3) Layer index base is inconsistent: Section 3.1 writes (n_l, b_l) for l = 1..L, but Eq. 4 uses w_l = sigma(k*(1 - l/(L-1) - tau)), which only makes sense 0-indexed - at l = L it returns a negative argument to the sigmoid - and the LOO discussion says 'restoring layers 0-10'. (4) 'Ph' is a row-category label in Table 2 that is never expanded anywhere in the caption or text (the reader must infer 'per-head' from Section 4's setup sentence, which is on the previous page). (5) 'LB' appears in Section 4 ('LB degrades 3-25'), Table 13, and Table 14 without ever being introduced as the abbreviation for LayerBudget. (6) 'zero-fill' first appears in Section 4.3 as 'the practical deployment setting' with no definition and no prior mention, in a paper whose contribution 3 is mean-fill; the reader is never told which of the two the headline tables use until they hunt through captions. (7) LayerBudget-KV is introduced in Related Work, four pages before the method it varies is defined, with a forward pointer to an appendix. (8) n_min = 'sink + recent' - neither the sink count nor the recent-window size is given numerically anywhere in the paper, so the allocator's starting point is unspecified. (9) B, the memory budget, has no stated units and no stated relation to the nominal CR the tables report; the whole of Appendix E exists because of this. (10) Q's units are never stated - it is a product of an attention-mass fraction, a cosine similarity, and an unnormalized sigmoid weight, then compared across layers as dQ/dM. (11) '118-119' in contribution 1 and Section 3.5 has no object: 118-119% of what? A greedy heuristic cannot exceed 100% of an optimum, so the referent is genuinely unrecoverable. (12) 'the Gini stability finding from Section [REF]' is invoked in Section 4.2 to explain the 32K results, but no Gini stability or calibration-transfer result appears anywhere in the main text. Twelve findings, well above the threshold of five.

Three recomputations from the paper's own stated inputs. (A) Motivating number, Section 1: 'At FP16, Llama-2-70B at 8K context requires over 40 GB'. Using the paper's own formula 2*L*S*H*d*b with L=80, S=8192, H=8 KV heads (Llama-2-70B is GQA), d=128, b=2 bytes: 2*80*8192*8*128*2 = 2.68e9 bytes = 2.68 GB. Even assuming 64 MHA heads: 2*80*8192*64*128*2 = 2.15e10 = 21.5 GB. The stated 40 GB is off by 15x (or 1.9x under the wrong architecture assumption). FAILS. (B) Section 3.5 concavity constants: 'dF(4->8) = 0.0035 > dF(8->16) = 0.0001'. From Appendix D: Mistral 0.9998 - 0.9794 = 0.0204; Llama-2-7B 0.9997 - 0.9758 = 0.0239; Llama-3.1-8B 0.9999 - 0.9817 = 0.0182; Qwen3-8B 0.9997 - 0.9683 = 0.0314. And dF(8->16) = 1.0000 - 0.9998 = 0.0002. The quoted 0.0035 is 5.8x-9x too small relative to the paper's own calibration table. FAILS. (C) The core mechanism claim, Section 3.5: 'at low CR, dQ/dM for a bit-upgrade exceeds that of a token-add at almost every layer'. From Eq. 2 (Q = C*F*w) and Eq. 3 (C = (n/S)^(1-g)) and M = 2*n*H*d*b/8: a 4->8 upgrade has dM = M and dQ = Q*(F(8)-F(4))/F(4), so dQ/dM = Q*0.0208/0.9794/M = 0.0213*Q/M. A token-add of dn has dM = M*dn/n and dQ ~ Q*(1-g)*dn/n, so dQ/dM = Q*(1-g)/M. Ratio (token-add : bit-upgrade) = (1-g)/0.0213 = 47*(1-g). At the paper's reported maximum Gini 0.93 this is 3.3; at its minimum 0.43 it is 27. Token-adds dominate bit-upgrades at EVERY layer in the reported Gini range, which is the exact opposite of the claim - and the discrepancy is worse, not better, if one uses the paper's own (erroneous) 0.0035 constant, which gives a ratio of 286*(1-g). FAILS. Also note (D): Table 16 at 'CR=2x' gives 287->218 MB = 1.32x, 189->54 = 3.50x, 95->54 = 1.76x - none equal 2x, contradicting Appendix E's '+/-0.05' audit claim. And the correct FP16 KV for Mistral-7B/Llama-3.1-8B at S=512 (32L, 8H, d=128) is 2*32*512*8*128*2 = 67.1 MB, matching neither the 95 MB nor the 189 MB in that table.

The most quotable number in the abstract is 'At 32K context on Mistral-7B, H2O at 4x collapses (83x PPL) while LayerBudget maintains 1.009x'. Two problems. First, the honest comparator in that same table (Table 21) is KIVI at 1.008 - fractionally BETTER than LayerBudget's 1.009 - and StreamingLLM at 1.026, so the 83x figure is chosen against the one baseline that fails, not against the one that is competitive. Second, several baselines in the paper appear misconfigured, which makes the whole ranking suspect: SnapKV scores 27.1/29.6/29.4/33.4 on MMLU (at or below four-choice chance) against Full KV 47.3/63.9/60.2/72.9, which is wildly out of line with SnapKV's published near-lossless MMLU behaviour, and unlike H2O it gets no reimplementation sanity check. DuoAttn is identical at all four CRs (1.22 x4 on Llama-2-7B) and MiniKV at 2/3/4x, i.e. those rows were not swept. Third, and in the other direction, KIVI's flat row means that at nominal 2x and 3x KIVI is actually spending ~4x-compressed bytes - roughly half LayerBudget's byte budget - and still ties, so LayerBudget's 2x 'win' of 0.01-0.02 PPL is achieved with double the memory. Fourth, the LongBench table has Full KV at 0.040-0.056, i.e. the reference itself is at the floor, and the caption concedes H2O's 0.097 is 'degenerate repetition inflating F1' - a benchmark that rewards degenerate output is not measuring what the claim needs. Verdict: the most favourable-sounding abstract number is not the honest one.

Internal contradictions found, all within the submitted text. (1) Same cell, three values: Llama-2-7B, 1024 tokens, mean-fill, 6x = 1.099 (Table 1), 1.17 (Table 2), 1.13 (Section 6). At 3x: 1.004 (Table 1) vs 1.02 (Table 2). At 4x on Mistral: 1.020 (Table 1) vs 1.03 (Table 2). (2) Table 2's caption asserts 'ranks 1st among all token-compression methods at every setting'; in that same table MiniKV beats LayerBudget on Llama-3.1-8B at 6x (1.07 vs 1.08) and ties on Qwen3-8B at 6x, and in Table 1 MoE-nD beats it on Mistral at 6x (1.038 vs 1.250), as does the authors' own LB-KV (1.062). (3) Abstract: '<=1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' vs Table 12's Llama-2-13B at 4x = 1.11 and 6x = 1.56. (4) Section 6: 'LayerBudget matches Full KV accuracy on every model (100...' vs Table 13's Mistral-7B Full KV 86.7 / LayerBudget-4x 73.3. (5) Configuration mislabelling: Table 5 (zero-fill, 512 tok) gives inverted-default 2.52 and sigmoid 45.09 on Llama-2-7B at 6x; Tables 17/18/19 report 'LayerBudget'/'Joint (Ours)' zero-fill as 45.09 and 3.23 - the sigmoid values - so the ablation and 'practical deployment' tables are not running the paper's stated default. (6) Appendix E asserts 'every method's effective CR matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05' while Table 16 at nominal 2x shows 1.32x/3.50x/1.76x. (7) Table 16 gives Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B identical KV geometry (Section 4) and identical compressed sizes but base KV differing by exactly 2x. (8) 'Memory-matched comparison in Appendix [REF]' is cited in the abstract, Section 4, and Table 17's caption; no such appendix is in the paper. (9) Section 4.3 calls zero-fill 'the practical deployment setting' while contribution 3 and all headline tables use mean-fill - the paper's own best configuration is declared impractical without explanation. (10) Section 4.2 cites 'the Gini stability finding from Section [REF]'; no such finding exists in the paper.

The prose has strong machine-generated signatures. (a) Negative parallelism used as a rhetorical default, at least seven times: 'the value is the measured ratio (not a typo)'; 'is allocator overhead, not a CR-denominator inconsistency between methods'; 'we treat inverted importance as a Mistral-tuned default, not a universal principle'; 'so the flat ~1.03 PPL across moderate CR is not solver degeneracy'; 'The two design points are therefore best read as complementary operating regimes of the same framework rather than two competing solvers'; 'allocates the joint budget at the request level rather than per-layer'; 'quality-gain-per-byte ... not the allocator alone'. (b) Uniform paragraph rhythm: nearly every subsection opens with a bolded assertion-as-header ('Key finding: LayerBudget remains near-lossless while uniform eviction collapses.', 'Importance direction is architecture-dependent.', 'Mean-fill preserves attention structure.', 'Signal crossover at high compression.', 'Component analysis.') followed by exactly one supporting number and one hedge. The Section 4 'Key findings' list is six bullets each built to the identical template. (c) Sections that describe rather than argue: Section 3.5 'Theoretical Properties' contains no property - it names MCKP, disclaims a bound it is not claiming, notes an FPTAS exists but is impractical, and stops. (d) Rebuttal material pasted into the paper: the ~400-word single paragraph in Related Work defending the MoE-nD and xKV reimplementations, ending 'any divergence from the original authors' reported numbers should be attributed to (a)... (b)... (c)... - we will update against their official code at camera-ready', reads as a response-to-reviewers, not as related work. Appendix E ends the same way: 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table [REF]'. Promising to fix the measurement after acceptance is not a paper sentence. (e) Jargon coined and used without definition in the same breath ('the MoE-nD framing', 'byte-CR reconciliation', 'the operating envelope', 'design point'). Verdict: yes, and the specific harm is that the argumentative sections have been replaced by descriptive ones.

(a) OVER-ASSERTION. 'Nearly all existing methods apply their strategy uniformly across layers' (Section 1) - contradicted one page later by the paper's own Related Work, which lists PyramidKV, D2O, SqueezeAttention, CAKE, Ada-KV, KVTuner and KVmix as per-layer or per-head. 'All evict tokens at full precision - none jointly optimize quantization' - contradicted three paragraphs later by MiniKV, EVICPRESS and MoE-nD. 'Uniform compression either under-compresses easy layers or degrades critical layers' - a universal disjunction, never measured. 'LayerBudget ranks 1st among all token-compression methods' and 'At every configuration across all four models ... it outperforms H2O, CAKE, SnapKV, D2O, and Ada-KV' - falsified in the same table by MiniKV. 'KV cache compression is most impactful at long context' - asserted as fact to justify a regime the paper mostly does not evaluate in. (b) VAGUE REFERENT. 'These results validate the Gini stability finding from Section [REF]' - there is no Gini stability finding; the referent does not exist. 'The reduction generalizes: at the same CR, logits KL drops from 0.6696 to 0.0636' - 'the reduction' has been described for one model at one CR and is then generalized on the strength of one more point. 'This is intrinsic to the byte budget' (Table 17 caption) - 'this' spans two preceding sentences with different subjects. 'achieving 118-119 [percent]' - the object of the percentage is absent, so the paper's first-listed contribution has no measurable content. 'the marginal-gain allocator absorbs both regimes' (abstract) - 'absorbs' is not defined and Table 12's 1.56 at 6x on the late-bottleneck model suggests it does not. (c) THING-VS-PROCESS CONFLATION. 'allocation' denotes both the plan {(n_l,b_l)} returned by Algorithm 1 and the act of computing it ('327K iterations per allocation'). 'profile'/'profiling' denotes both the Gini statistics artifact ('fixed profiles (calibrated once per model)') and the collection procedure ('the full profiling pipeline adds 61-109'). 'importance' denotes both the weight w_l and the LOO-measured empirical sensitivity, which is precisely the conflation that makes Section 3.2's architecture-dependence discussion hard to follow. 'compression ratio' denotes both the requested target and the achieved byte ratio - Appendix E exists solely because of this conflation and still does not fix Table 16. (d) FALSE PRECISION. '118-119' quoted to 1pp on an unstated base. 'Pearson rho = 0.194' computed over TinyLlama-1.1B's 22 layers and used to conclude the signals are complementary: at n=22, rho=0.194 has p~0.39 and a 95% CI spanning roughly [-0.25, 0.56], so it is statistically indistinguishable both from 0 and from a moderate correlation - the conclusion does not follow from the number. 'MAE 3.1' reported with no sample count and on one model. 'reduces output distortion by 96' from a single model at a single CR (0.249 -> 0.009). PPL ratios reported to three decimals (1.000 vs 1.006 vs 1.009) from n=6 WikiText-2 chunks with no confidence interval, while Section 4 explicitly argues variance need not be reported. NIAH percentages of 86.7 / 73.3 / 93.3 / 46.7 are multiples of 1/15, so the headline 'LayerBudget 100 vs KIVI 93.3' is 15/15 vs 14/15 - a one-trial difference presented as a categorical distinction between method families.

Thesis, reconstructed without headings: 'Choosing token-retention count and KV bit-width jointly per layer, quantizing before evicting, gives near-lossless KV cache compression at 2-4x across model scales.' Topic sentences map to the thesis in Sections 1, 3.1-3.4, 4.1, 4.2, 5 and 6. Paragraphs that map to neither the thesis nor their own evidence: (1) The MoE-nD/xKV paragraph in Related Work. Its topic sentence is about a concurrent work's formulation; its body is a defence of the authors' own reimplementations, a concession that they lose at 6x, an announcement of an unpublished variant, and a promise to rerun at camera-ready. It argues neither for the thesis nor for the topic sentence. Candidate for deletion and replacement by a two-sentence positioning note plus an honest table. (2) Section 3.5 'Theoretical Properties'. I cannot identify a topic sentence that the paragraph then supports: it opens by classifying the objective as MCKP, spends its body explaining which guarantee is NOT claimed and why an FPTAS is impractical, and closes with an empirical percentage whose object is missing. Per the probe instruction, a paragraph whose topic sentence cannot be identified is itself the finding. (3) Appendix E in its entirety. Its topic is 'two of our tables use different memory denominators and the one in Table 15 is inflated 2x; we will regenerate it for camera-ready'. That is an erratum, not a contribution, and it is load-bearing for the memory-matched claim it does not actually establish. (4) The 'Compression ratio (CR) definition' paragraph in Section 4 promises to 'flag every cell in our results tables where method-byte CR diverges from token-count CR' - no such flags appear in any table, so the paragraph's evidence does not map to its own topic sentence. (5) Section 3.3's 'Weak correlation enables complementary allocation' paragraph: the topic sentence claims complementarity enables the method, but the evidence is one Pearson coefficient on TinyLlama-1.1B, a model that appears in no experiment in the paper. Its evidence does not map to its topic sentence, and neither maps to the thesis, which is about 7B-72B models.

I received only LaTeX source, not a compiled PDF, so I could not examine any figure as rendered - ppl_scaling.pdf, allocation_heatmap.pdf and signal_curves.pdf were unverifiable. I flag that as a gap in my review. What I can assess from source and captions is still problematic. (1) The paper has three figures for a nine-page systems paper and none of them depicts the method: there is no pipeline or architecture figure, so a first-time reader must reconstruct the allocator from prose plus a nine-line pseudocode box (Algorithm 1) whose inner loop is a single line, 'Compute dQ/dM for action'. (2) Two of the three figures (allocation_heatmap, signal_curves) are on TinyLlama-1.1B, a model that appears nowhere in the seven-model evaluation - the only visualizations of the paper's core mechanism are on a model whose results are never reported. (3) Both are placed in 0.48-textwidth minipages carrying, respectively, a per-layer bar chart with color-encoded precision over 22 layers plus a dashed Gini overlay, and a two-series curve plot - at half column width with a two-line caption, the per-layer heatmap in particular is very likely illegible; this needs to be checked in the PDF. (4) Figure 1's caption claims 'GQA models (solid) are more robust than MHA (dashed)' and 'Qwen2.5-72B achieves 1.004 at 4x', but Table 22 reports Qwen2.5-72B at 4x as 1.00, not 1.004 - the caption's precision exceeds the table's. (5) The document contains an unclosed table environment ('begin{table[t]') immediately before the importance-direction table, which would abort compilation, so I cannot be confident any figure or table renders at all.

(a) ANONYMITY: no institution, no funding acknowledgment, no identifying self-citation, no non-anonymous link. Two minor items: the repeated first-person disclosure of submission timing ('the official artifacts were not public at submission time', 'we will update against their official code at camera-ready', 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table [REF]') is not de-anonymizing but does put unfinished work on the record inside the submission; and the priority framing in Related Work ('The closest concurrent work is MoE-nD, which independently arrives at the same formulation') is assertive but not aggressive. No desk-reject risk on anonymity. (b) COMPLETENESS: the checklist is included only as 'input{checklist}' - I cannot verify that the mandatory NeurIPS paper checklist is present and answered, nor that the LLM-usage item is addressed. Given the prose signatures documented in P6, an unanswered LLM-usage item would be a compliance problem; this is unverifiable from what I was given and must be checked. (c) FORMAT: this is where the real risk is. The source contains at least three unbalanced-brace faults that would abort a LaTeX run - 'begin{table[t]' (importance ablation table), 'section{Analysis' (Section 6 header), 'textbf{Downstream accuracy.' (Section 6 paragraph header). Downstream of these, the abstract terminates mid-sentence ('retains 100'), the Limitations block has no section heading and is preceded by a sentence cut off at 'On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]', and roughly thirty numeric claims across the abstract, contributions, results and ablations terminate immediately after a percent sign - the pattern of an unescaped '%' commenting out the rest of each line, which would silently delete that text from the compiled PDF. Page limit (9 content pages) could not be verified without compiling, but the main text carries Sections 1-7 plus two full-width tables, three figures and one ablation table, so it is at or near the limit. Recommendation: this must be compiled and read end-to-end before any submission; as received it is a desk-reject risk on format.

(a) What the algorithm actually computes: Algorithm 1 initializes every layer at (n_min = sink+recent, b_min = 4), then repeatedly applies whichever (layer, action) maximizes dQ/dM until the byte budget B is exhausted, where Q(l,n,b) = (n/S)^(1-g_l) * F(b) * sigma(k*(1 - l/(L-1) - tau)) and M(n,b) = 2*n*H*d*b/8. (b) Does that equal the object the theory names? No, on three counts. First, Section 3.5 calls this 'an instance of the multiple-choice knapsack problem' and invokes an FPTAS for MCKP. MCKP requires selecting exactly one item from each class; here n_l is quasi-continuous (step size 8, up to S) and b_l has three levels, so the problem is a bounded/multi-dimensional knapsack, and the cited FPTAS does not apply as stated. The identification is asserted, never shown. Second, Q is never connected to any measured quality. F(b) is a cosine similarity between quantized and full-precision tensors; C is a fraction of attention mass; w_l is an unnormalized sigmoid with hand-set k=5, tau=0.3. Their product has no units and is never validated as a monotone predictor of PPL or task accuracy - yet the entire claim rests on maximizing it. Contribution 1's phrase 'calibrated fidelity constants' therefore overstates Appendix D, which calibrates F as cosine similarity and nothing more. Third, and most seriously, the paper's central behavioural claim does not follow from its own objective. Section 3.5 states 'quantize first' emerges from the marginal gains because 'dQ/dM for a bit-upgrade exceeds that of a token-add at almost every layer'. Recomputing from Eq. 2-3 and Appendix D: bit-upgrade dQ/dM = Q*(F8-F4)/F4/M = 0.0213*Q/M; token-add dQ/dM = Q*(1-g_l)/M. Token-adds win by 47*(1-g_l), which is >3x even at the paper's maximum Gini of 0.93. Under the stated model the allocator would essentially never upgrade bits. (c) Semantics silently changed: the coverage law C = (n/S)^(1-g) is asserted 'approximately' with no derivation and has degenerate boundary behaviour - at g -> 1 it returns C = 1 for any n >= 1, i.e. it claims that retaining a single token captures all attention mass, which is false unless attention is exactly a delta. Since g_l is measured from the last-token attention row only (an O(S) shortcut), a layer whose last-token attention is sparse but whose full attention matrix is not will be assigned near-total coverage at near-zero token count. This is a load-bearing assumption validated once, on one model, by a single MAE number. Verdict: what is run does not match what is argued, in the specific place the paper's title claim lives.

Contributions in the order claimed, with the isolating experiment and its measured marginal effect. (C1) 'Quantize-first greedy solver with calibrated fidelity constants, achieving 118-119 [percent of an unstated base]'. Isolating experiment: Table 17 (A1 component analysis). Measured effect: Joint (Ours) 1.00/3.23 on Mistral and 1.02/45.09 on Llama-2 at 3x/6x, versus Quant only 1.00/1.00 and 1.02/1.01. The joint solver is exactly equal to quant-only at 3x and 3.2x-45x WORSE at 6x, and it is also slightly worse than Eviction only at 6x (3.18 / 44.71). The paper's first and primary contribution has a measured marginal effect of zero at the CR where the paper claims to work and a large negative effect elsewhere. Additionally the headline '118-119' has no stated object, so it cannot be checked at all. This is the fatal P12 pattern. (C2) 'Inverted importance improves 6x compression by 60-94'. Isolating experiment: Table 5. Measured effect: real and large (Llama-2-7B 6x: inverted 2.52 vs flat 5.94 vs sigmoid 45.09). But it only acts at 6x, the regime the paper's own Table 17 shows is dominated by quant-only, and Section 3.2 concedes the direction is Mistral-specific (Llama-2-13B late-bottleneck, Qwen2.5-14B flat). So the measured effect is confined to a regime where the method loses anyway, and the mechanism is a per-model hyperparameter, not a principle. (C3) 'Mean-fill reduces output KL by 96'. Isolating evidence: Section 6 (KL 0.249->0.009 Mistral; 0.6696->0.0636 Llama-2) and the zero-fill vs mean-fill table pair. Largest measured marginal effect in the paper - but the credit is confounded: the '45.09 -> 1.13' improvement attributed to mean-fill is measured against a zero-fill number (45.09) that Table 5 assigns to the SIGMOID variant, whereas the inverted default at zero-fill is 2.52. So the true mean-fill effect at 6x on Llama-2-7B is 2.52 -> 1.13, not 45.09 -> 1.13. (C4) '17-baseline controlled comparison, ranks 1st among methods that reduce token count'. The category is constructed to exclude the one baseline that wins; and the claim is falsified inside Table 2 by MiniKV at Llama-3.1-8B 6x. (C5) '16K-32K validation'. LayerBudget 1.009 vs KIVI 1.008 at 32K/4x on Mistral - KIVI is fractionally better; on Llama-3.1-8B they tie at 1.035. Marginal effect vs the honest baseline: zero or negative. (C6) '72B scaling, 1.004 at 4x'. Table 22: KIVI 1.00 at every CR including 6x, LayerBudget 1.06 at 6x; RULER at 2x KIVI 99 vs LayerBudget 98. Marginal effect vs baseline: zero or negative. Verdict: the ranking by measured marginal effect is C3 > C2 >> C1 = C5 = C6 = 0, while the abstract and contribution list present C1 first as the paper's identity. The honest restructuring is to lead with mean-fill (a KV-eviction trick that helps every eviction method, including the baselines) and demote the joint allocator.

(a) One-sentence contribution in this community's vocabulary: 'A training-free, online, per-layer allocator that jointly selects token-retention counts and KV bit-widths under a global memory budget via greedy marginal gain.' That sentence is stateable, so the venue-fit test passes on framing - the paper belongs at NeurIPS/ICLR/MLSys, not elsewhere. (b) Terms a PC member would have to look up or would not use: 'mean-fill' and 'zero-fill' (the paper's coinages; the standard framing is padding or masking of evicted slots), 'inverted importance', 'the MoE-nD framing' (a framing is not a baseline), 'coverage law', 'fidelity constants', 'byte-CR reconciliation', 'operating envelope', 'design point', 'LB-KV', and the unexplained 'Ph' row label. None is disqualifying but the density is high for a paper whose core idea is simple. (c) No mechanism belongs to a different community; there is no misrouting to report. (d) This is where the fit problem is real. The related work positions almost entirely against 2024-2025 methods (H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, StreamingLLM, KIVI, KVQuant) plus two 2026 arXiv preprints reimplemented by the authors. It does not engage the published 2026 bar at this venue's sibling conferences - KVTC (ICLR 2026, 20-40x), STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight, 20x), DefensiveKV/Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026, RULER 91.4 at 20% cache), TurboQuant (ICLR 2026) - nor the directly-overlapping RDKV and HqeKV, nor NVIDIA KVPress as the standard harness, nor the current benchmark set (LongBench-v2, RULER 4K-128K, InfiniteBench, SCBench). A committee reading '2-4x near-lossless, collapses at 6x' against a field that has published 14-20x near-lossless will not see the delta. So: correct room, but the paper argues against the room as it was two years ago. I report this as a major weakness, not a stylistic note.

(a) Expected metrics for KV-cache compression as of 2026: WikiText-2/PG19 PPL (REPORTED, n=6 chunks); RULER 4K-128K, 13 subtasks (REPORTED only as two columns at 4096 on Qwen2.5-72B - effectively OMITTED); LongBench-v2 (OMITTED; v1 reported but with Full KV at 0.040-0.056, i.e. at the floor); InfiniteBench (OMITTED); SCBench, the KV-cache-centric benchmark (OMITTED); NIAH (REPORTED, but at 15 trials per cell); MMLU (REPORTED); GSM8K (REPORTED, n=200); effective bits per token, the field's common currency for mixed-precision methods (OMITTED - striking for a method whose output is a per-layer bit assignment); decode throughput / attention speedup (REPORTED and NEGATIVE: Table 16's own footnote says 'Speedup <1x due to compression overhead', and TPOT overhead is +2.6% to +12.2%); peak memory or max-batch/max-context enabled (OMITTED - only cache bytes are reported); dequantization kernel cost and whether a fused mixed-bit decode path exists (OMITTED). (b) Claim-reversing omissions: yes. The abstract's ranking claim is 'at memory-matched comparison', and the memory-matched experiment is not in the paper; the one memory table that exists (Table 15) reverses the claim against KIVI. RULER and LongBench-v2 at real context lengths would directly test the 'near-lossless' claim and are absent or degenerate. Effective bits/token would make the KIVI comparison trivially checkable and is absent. (c) Unmeasured terms in the paper's own objective: Q = C * F * w is the thing being maximized, and only C is ever validated (attention-mass MAE 3.1 on one model); F is validated as cosine similarity but never mapped to any quality metric; w is never validated at all - its direction is probed by LOO on three models that disagree, and k=5, tau=0.3 are never swept. A quality model whose two of three factors are never checked against quality is an unmeasured objective term. (d) Workload regime mismatch: the claims are stated over the long-context memory-pressure regime ('KV cache compression is most impactful at long context'), but the main table, both head-to-heads, all ablations, MMLU, GSM8K and NIAH are at 512-4096 tokens; only one table reaches 16K-32K, covering 3 models, 2 CRs and 4 methods, with the 32K Qwen3-8B cells OOM. At the regime where nearly all the numbers were taken (Mistral-7B, 1024 tokens, ~134 MB of FP16 KV against a 4-bit weight footprint of several GB), the KV cache is not the bottleneck the paper opens by describing. Also, all models are run with 4-bit weights and the interaction between weight quantization and the KV-compression conclusions is never isolated.
